item.title: Galois Groups of Shifted Exponential Polynomials
item.description: arXiv:2610.26873v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For a fixed integer $a>0$, consider the shifted truncations \[ F_{n,a}(x)=\sum_{j=0}^{n}\frac{x^j}{(a+j)!} \] and their monic integral normalizations $P_{n,a}(x)=(n+a)!F_{n,a}(x)$. In this paper, we prove that, for every fixed integer $a>0$, the set of $n$ for which $F_{n,a}$ is irreducible has natural density one. We also prove that $G_{n,a}:=\text{Gal}(F_{n,a}/\mathbb{Q})$ is primitive for all sufficiently large $n$ for which $F_{n,a}$ is irreducible, and that it contains $A_n$ for a density-one set of $n$. Finally, we prove that, for any fixed integer $a>0$, the discriminant of $F_{n,a}$ is a nonsquare for a density-one set of $n$, and hence that $\text{Gal}(F_{n,a}/\mathbb{Q})=S_n$ for a density-one set of $n$. To obtain irreducibility with density one, we use a result of Shorey and Tijdeman, as well as a smooth-number density argument. Following that, two explicitly chosen Newton polygons give cycles that force primitivity, and hence containment of $A_n$. Finally, an exact computation of the valuation of the discriminant at primes satisfying $\frac n2+a<p<n+a$ implies that the discriminant is a nonsquare for odd $a$ and almost all $n$, implying the group is $S_n$ in those cases. For even $a$, we contradict the existence of many square discriminants by showing they generate a family of biased Dirichlet characters. These imply many zeros off of the critical line, which contradict standard zero-density bounds.
item.dc:creator: Shachar Weinbaum

item.title: Class polynomial obstructions to canonical congruences for the smallest parts function
item.description: arXiv:2610.27145v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We resolve an open conjecture by proving that the only "canonical'' Ramanujan congruence primes for the Andrews' smallest parts function, $\operatorname{spt}(n)$, are $\ell= 5, 7, 13$. Building on work of Ahlgren and Kim, we show that any such congruence forces square-index coefficients of certain weakly holomorphic forms of weight $1/2$ to vanish modulo the congruence prime. A normalized Borcherds product converts this into the vanishing of the derivative of a quotient of two oriented CM polynomials on $X_0(6)$. A quaternionic volume estimate in an Eichler order of level $6$ prevents that vanishing when a suitable inert discriminant is small. Trevi\~no's character estimate supplies such a discriminant for every prime at least $10^{11}$. The remaining range is covered by the previous calculations of Ahlgren and Kim. These results have been verified in Lean by AxiomProver.
item.dc:creator: Larry Rolen

item.title: Small sums of roots of unity: polylogarithmic exceptional sets and conditional separation
item.description: arXiv:2610.27231v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove a polylogarithmic exceptional-set estimate for symmetric five-term sums of roots of unity of arbitrary order. More precisely, at most $O((\log(2N))^{11})$ points of the $N$-grid satisfy $|1+2\cos(2\pi x)+2\cos(2\pi y)|<\exp(-C(\log(2N))^{13})$. This implies the corresponding bound for small conjugates at the reduced conductor: outside polylogarithmically many real embeddings, every such sum is at least quasipolynomially large. The proof is unconditional and combines a polynomial-vector-field multiplicity estimate, arithmetic jet determinants, analytic propagation, and interpolation determinants for nearby grid points. As a companion result, assuming a uniform number-field $abc$ conjecture, we prove that every sum of a fixed number of distinct prime-order roots of unity has modulus at least $\exp(-\varepsilon p)$ for every $\varepsilon>0$ and all sufficiently large primes $p$, uniformly in the exponents. That proof uses simultaneous compression of the exponents, discriminant estimates, and cyclic resultants.
item.dc:creator: Qi Cheng

item.title: Upper Bounds on the de Bruijn-Newman constant for Dirichlet $L$-functions with primitive real-valued characters
item.description: arXiv:2610.27343v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $\chi_m$ be a primitive real-valued Dirichlet character of conductor $m\ge3$, let $L(s)=L(s,\chi_m)$ be the associated Dirichlet $L$-function, and let $\xi_L(s)$ denote its completed form. For each $t \in \mathbb R,$ we define the entire function \[ H^L_t(z) := \int_{-\infty}^{\infty} e^{tu^2}\, \Phi_L(u)\, e^{izu}\, du, \] where $\Phi_L$ is the superexponentially decaying density \[ \Phi_L(u) := \frac{1}{2\pi}\int_{-\infty}^{\infty} \xi_L\!\left(\frac{1+is}{2}\right) e^{-isu}\, ds. \] The family $\{H_t^L\}_{t \in \mathbb R}$ describes the heat-flow evolution of $\xi_L$ and solves a backward heat equation. By the work of Newman, there exists a finite constant $\Lambda_L$, called the generalized de Bruijn--Newman constant, such that all the zeros of $H_t^L$ are real if and only if $t \ge \Lambda_L$. The Generalized Riemann Hypothesis (GRH) for $L$ is equivalent to the assertion that $\Lambda_L \le 0$. Dobner established the matching lower bound $\Lambda_L \ge 0$, while de Bruijn proved the upper bound $\Lambda_L \le \tfrac12$. We prove the unconditional uniform bound $\Lambda_L\le953/3200=0.2978125$ for every primitive real-valued character of conductor $3\le m\le400$, together with stronger individual bounds. The proof extends the effective approximation of Polymath to Dirichlet $L$-functions, retaining the conductor dependence in the error estimates. We combine these estimates with Platt's numerical verification of GRH by Platt and rigorous interval computations. We also give conditional bounds under explicit global initial zero-strip hypotheses, including $|\operatorname{Im}z|\le3/4$ for the zeros of $H_0^L$.
item.dc:creator: Ricardo Freire, Cristian Gonz\'alez-Riquelme, Claudio Mu\~noz, Felipe Poblete, Vicente Salinas

item.title: The Projective Reed-Muller Code from Quartic Curves in the Projective Plane
item.description: arXiv:2610.27392v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the Hamming weight enumerator of the projective Reed-Muller code $\mathcal C_{2,4}$ over $\mathbf F_q$, with $\operatorname{char}(\mathbf F_q)>3$. We determine the geometrically reducible and singular contributions by combining incidence counts with counts of plane linear series on a fixed normalization. The line and conic configurations and the genus zero cases give explicit polynomials. The line-cubic and genus one cases give formulas involving class numbers. The genus two contribution is a finite sum over hyperelliptic models, using their point counts over $\mathbf F_q$ and $\mathbf F_{q^2}$ and their rational Weierstrass points. The remaining smooth contribution is the weighted point count distribution of nonhyperelliptic genus three curves.
item.dc:creator: Xu Zhuang

item.title: Quantum Variance for Hecke--Maass Cusp Forms on the Vertical Geodesic
item.description: arXiv:2610.27454v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $X=\mathrm{PSL}_2(\mathbb Z)\backslash\mathbb H$, and let $\{u_j\}$ be an orthonormal basis of even Hecke--Maass cusp forms on $X$ with Laplace eigenvalues $1/4+t_j^2$. For a real-valued $\psi\in C_c^\infty(0,\infty)$, define \[ \mu_j(\psi)=\int_0^\infty\psi(y)|u_j(iy)|^2\,\frac{dy}{y}, \qquad M(\psi)=\frac6\pi\int_0^\infty\psi(y)\,\frac{dy}{y}. \] For $T\ge2$, $1\le U\le T$, and every $\varepsilon>0$, we prove \[ \sum_{\substack{u_j\ {\rm even}\\T<t_j\le T+U}} L(1,\mathrm{sym}^2u_j)|\mu_j(\psi)-M(\psi)|^2 \ll_{\psi,\varepsilon}T^{1+\varepsilon}. \] As a consequence, for fixed $0<\theta\le1$, $0<\eta<\theta/2$, and every $\varepsilon>0$, if $T^\theta\le U\le T$, then all but \[ O_{\psi,\theta,\eta,\varepsilon} \!\left(T^{1+2\eta+\varepsilon}\right) \] of the even forms with $T<t_j\le T+U$ satisfy $\mu_j(\psi)=M(\psi)+O(T^{-\eta})$. In particular, the exceptional proportion tends to zero in this short spectral interval.
item.dc:creator: Qingfeng Sun, Qizhi Zhang

item.title: Bowen--Franks groups and minus class groups of imaginary abelian fields
item.description: arXiv:2610.27481v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: $\mathrm{Lei}$, $\mathrm{M\ddot{u}ller}$, and $\mathrm{Valli\grave{e}res}$ constructed a directed graph for which the torsion part of the corresponding Bowen--Franks group is related to the minus part of the class group of a cyclotomic number field with prime conductor. We extend this result to a general imaginary abelian field.
item.dc:creator: Takuya Murakami

item.title: Non-vanishing of central values of angular Hecke $L$-functions
item.description: arXiv:2610.27493v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we evaluate asymptotically the first and second moment of central values of the family of Hecke $L$-functions associated to angular characters over imaginary quadratic number fields of class number one. We use our results to deduce a non-vanishing result concerning these $L$-functions.
item.dc:creator: Peng Gao

item.title: On a Notion of Density Related to Restricted Diophantine Approximation
item.description: arXiv:2610.27497v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce notion of density for a subset of the natural numbers called the Diophantine density. First, we demonstrate that the Diophantine density is an abstract density in the sense of Di Nasso and Jin. Then we establish upper and lower bounds for the Diophantine density of a set and its complement respectively. We also exhibit a construction which allows us to find a set whose density can be any value between zero and one. Finally, we prove a restricted-denominator analog of Dirichlet's approximation theorem for sets of non-zero Diophantine density.
item.dc:creator: Chance Sanford

item.title: An Equivariant Main Conjecture for Branched $\mathbb Z_p$-Towers of Finite Graphs and Applications
item.description: arXiv:2610.27551v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $p$ be a prime and let $Y/X$ be a finite abelian branched cover of finite connected graphs. We consider a compatible branched $\mathbb Z_p$-tower above $Y$ whose total Galois group over $X$ is abelian. We construct an equivariant Picard Iwasawa module over the completed group ring of the total Galois group and give an explicit presentation of this module. On the analytic side, we construct an equivariant Artin--Ihara $L$-element at the top of the tower and isolate a modified factor whose value at $u=1$ is well defined. Our main result computes the Fitting ideal of the equivariant Picard Iwasawa module in terms of these special values and augmentation ideals determined by the inertia groups. As applications, we recover the main conjecture for branched $\mathbb Z_p$-towers from our earlier work and obtain finite-level Fitting-ideal and annihilation formulas which can be viewed as graph-theoretic analogues of the conjectures of Kurihara and Brumer--Stark.
item.dc:creator: Rusiru Gambheera

item.title: Small values of the Riemann zeta-function near the critical line
item.description: arXiv:2610.27591v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Assuming the Riemann Hypothesis, we study negative moments and small values of the Riemann zeta-function to the right of the critical line. For every fixed $0<k<1/2$, we establish the conjecturally sharp bound $$ \frac1T\int_T^{2T} \Big|\zeta(\tfrac12+\alpha+it)\Big|^{-2k}\,dt \ll \alpha^{-k^2}, $$ for $\alpha=o(1)$ and $\alpha\gg 1/\log T$. We also obtain almost sharp upper bounds slightly to the left of $1/\log T$. This improves the upper bounds of the first two authors for shifts as small as $1/\log T$, confirming a conjecture of Gonek in this range. A separate bound for the moment at $k=1/2$ yields an improved bound for cancellation in the M\"obius function. Namely, we show that $$ \sum_{n\leq x}\mu(n) \ll \sqrt{x}\exp \bigg(C\sqrt{\frac{\log x}{\log\log x}}\bigg) $$ for some $C>0$, improving on previous results of Soundararajan, Balazard and de Roton, and of the first two authors. For $t$ chosen uniformly from $[T,2T]$, we also prove that \[ \min_{|h|\leq1} \Big|\zeta\Big(\tfrac12+\alpha+i(t+h)\Big)\Big| =\alpha^{1+o(1)} \] in probability, provided that $\alpha \ll (\log T)^{-c}$ for some fixed $c >0$, and $\alpha\log T/\log\log T\to\infty$. This agrees with the leading order predicted by a minimum analogue of the Fyodorov--Hiary--Keating Conjecture. Further results include bounds for minima on intervals of logarithmically growing length, for negative moments in almost all short intervals, and an extension of the range of sharp negative-moment bounds for $k>1/2$. A main ingredient in the proof of some of these results is a Gaussian large-deviation upper bound for $\log|\zeta(1/2+\alpha+it)|^{-1}$, obtained by building on work of Arguin, Bailey, and Roberts.
item.dc:creator: Hung M. Bui, Alexandra Florea, Andr\'e Heycock

item.title: A determinant formula for multiple harmonic sums and their linear independence
item.description: arXiv:2610.27767v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We explicitly evaluate a family of determinants whose entries are multiple harmonic sums. As a consequence, we prove that certain finite sequences of multiple harmonic sums are linearly independent. This result strengthens the previously known linear independence of the corresponding infinite sequences and stands in contrast to the abundance of linear relations among multiple zeta values.
item.dc:creator: Minoru Hirose, Hideki Murahara, Shingo Saito

item.title: Dense Sets with Prescribed Difference Representation Functions
item.description: arXiv:2610.27786v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For a set $A$ of positive integers, let $d_A(n)$ denote the number of representations of $n$ as a difference of two elements of $A$. We prove that, if $\liminf_{n\to\infty}f(n)\geq2$, then for every Sidon set $B$ and every positive function $\omega(x)$ tending to infinity there is a set $A\subseteq\N$ such that $d_A(n)=f(n)$ for all $n\in\N$ and $|A(x)-B(x/2)|\leq\omega(x)$ for all $x\geq1$. We also give two extensions that allow $f(n)=1$ for infinitely many $n$. For an infinite Sidon set $B$, the same density scale $B(x/2)$ is retained when $f$ is at least $2$ on arbitrarily long intervals centered at elements of $2B$. If $\{n:f(n)\geq2\}$ contains arbitrarily long intervals, the density scale $B(x/3)$ is obtained for every Sidon set $B$. The proofs use remote insertion of new representations together with controlled deletions from a Sidon core. As a quantitative consequence, Ruzsa's dense infinite Sidon sequence gives $A(x)=x^{\sqrt2-1+o(1)}$ whenever $\{n:f(n)\geq2\}$ contains arbitrarily long intervals.
item.dc:creator: Wu-Xia Ma, Bing-Ling Wu

item.title: New Directions in Irrationality
item.description: arXiv:2610.27799v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Since Ap\'ery's proof of the irrationality of $\zeta(3)$, decades of work have explored integrals, hypergeometric identities, and recurrences with exceptional arithmetic properties, to discover the strongest quantitative bounds on irrationality measures for zeta values and related constants. Yet, most findings have relied on specially tailored families of such constructions, making their systematic extension difficult. Here we show how these constructions can be connected and generalized into a common multidimensional structure based on conservative matrix fields (CMFs), enabling a systematic discovery of new irrationality proofs and quantitative bounds for irrationality exponents. CMFs are finite-dimensional cocycles of compatible rational matrix shifts, and are shown to capture all the classical constructions developed since Ap\'ery as one-dimensional trajectories. The initial point encodes the mathematical constants; varying the trajectory within a suitable convergence region produces different approximation schemes for the same constants. We use this structure to improve the irrationality measures of famous constants, yielding for example $\mu(\zeta(2))<4.62675$ and $\mu(\zeta(3))<5.4197$, and proving that $1,\zeta(3),\zeta(4)$ are linearly independent over $\mathbb{Q}$, yielding $\mu(A\zeta(3)+B\zeta(4))<66.3$ for every $(A,B)\in\mathbb{Q}^2\setminus\{(0,0)\}$. The same approach demonstrated over other CMFs provides irrationality proving trajectories for infinitely more mathematical constants. We further construct higher-rank CMFs with explicit initial states for $1,\zeta(2),\zeta(3),\ldots,\zeta(d+1)$, and identify the arithmetic conditions needed to obtain further, higher-order independence results.
item.dc:creator: Elyasheev Leibtag, Hila Barkan, Rotem Kalisch, Shachar Weinbaum, Michael Shalyt, Ido Kaminer

item.title: Weyl Bounds for $\operatorname{GL}_2\times \operatorname{GL}_2$ Rankin--Selberg $L$-functions via Short Spectral Moments
item.description: arXiv:2610.27804v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $f$ and $g$ be Hecke--Maass cusp forms of $\operatorname{SL}_2(\mathbb{Z})$, with spectral parameters $t_f$ and $t_g$, respectively. Let $T$ be a large parameter and put $L = |T-t_g|.$ We prove the Lindel\"of-on-average estimate \[ \sum_{ |t_f-T|\leq H} \left|L\!\left(\frac12,f\otimes g\right)\right|^2 \ll_{\varepsilon} T^{1+\varepsilon}H, \] uniformly in the range \[ T^{1/3+\varepsilon}\ll H,\qquad HT^\varepsilon\ll L\leq T. \] As an immediate consequence, in the generic range when both $|t_g|$ and $L$ are of size $T$, we obtain the Weyl bound \[ L\!\left(\frac12,f\otimes g\right) \ll_\varepsilon C(f\times g)^{1/6+\varepsilon}. \]
item.dc:creator: Zihao Wang

item.title: Primes in short intervals assuming the Riemann hypothesis
item.description: arXiv:2610.27830v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In 2001 Baker, Harman, and Pintz proved, for $x$ sufficiently large, the existence of at least one prime in the sub-linear interval $[x,x+x^{\frac{1}{2} +\frac{1}{40}}]$. But just how large is sufficiently large? In the current note I shall make the Baker--Harman--Pintz theorem effective, but at an extremely high price. Contingent upon assuming validity of the Riemann hypothesis (RH), I shall show that the Baker--Harman--Pintz theorem holds for $x \geq 3.5\times 10^{90}$. Furthermore, again assuming RH, I shall also show that for any $0< m\leq15.831$ and $x \geq 1$ there is at least one prime in the interval $[x,x+x^{\frac{1}{2} +\frac{1}{m}}]$, and that for $M\geq 2.29$ and $y \geq 1$ there is at least one prime in the interval $[y^M, (y+1)^M]$.
item.dc:creator: Matt Visser (Victoria University of Wellington)

item.title: Post-quantum commutative group actions from oriented superspecial abelian varieties
item.description: arXiv:2610.27922v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the cryptographic use of Shimura class group actions on superspecial principally polarized abelian varieties equipped with a CM orientation, within the context of post-quantum cryptography. Besides giving an accessible introduction to the topic, illustrated with many examples, we provide tools for representing CM orientations through higher-dimensional isogenies and for computing the Shimura class group action in the restricted effective group action model. Here, key auxiliary results are a version of Kani's lemma "with CM" and a trick that often allows to halve the ambient dimension. We also give a method for finding superspecial principally polarized abelian surfaces that are oriented by a given CM order, which is extracted from an algebraic framework for studying CM orientations using the Ibukiyama-Katsura-Oort correspondence. We also analyze obstructions to transitivity of the Shimura class group action, related to the characteristic-zero notion of CM type.
item.dc:creator: Wouter Castryck, Bogdan Adrian Dina, P\'eter Kutas, Gioella Lorenzon

item.title: Theta Relations
item.description: arXiv:2610.27959v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Motivated by the classical quartic and cubic theta identities, we establish a product formula for Siegel--Jacobi theta series associated with rationally isometric positive-definite quadratic spaces. Our main theorem expresses a product of theta series of arbitrary Siegel degree as a finite double character sum over quotients of commensurable lattices. For the root lattice $A_2$, it yields a finite Fourier identity for cubes of cubic theta functions, a new proof of the two-variable cubic identity, and seven independent relations in degree two. A second specialization gives a new square analogue of the two-variable cubic identity. At the origin it reduces to $a(q)a(q^2)=b(q)b(q^2)+c(q)c(q^2)$; in degree two, the same seven relation patterns recur with each cube replaced by the corresponding product at $\tau$ and $2\tau$. We further extend the cubic identities on $A_2$ to $\ell$-th-power identities on $A_{\ell-1}$ for every $\ell\geq3$, and to $2\ell$-th-power identities on $A_{\ell-1}$ for every $\ell\geq2$, in arbitrary Siegel degree. The doubled-order construction recovers Jacobi's quartic identity and gives its analogues in arbitrary Siegel degree.
item.dc:creator: Rong Chen, Haigang Zhou, Xiao-Jie Zhu

item.title: SEAC from EAC modulo Schanuel: reduction to algebraic exponentials
item.description: arXiv:2610.27963v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider the problem of reducing Zilber's pseudo-exponentiation conjecture to mere exponential-algebraic closedness, assuming Schanuel's conjecture but not Zilber-Pink. Generalising work of Mantova, we show that it would suffice to show that perfectly rotund varieties have non-dense intersection with finitely generated subgroups of the graph of exponentiation in which the exponentials live in a number field.
item.dc:creator: Martin Bays

item.title: Uncountably many settled elements are never Frobenius elements
item.description: arXiv:2610.27997v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Boston and Jones conjectured that given a number field $K$, a quadratic polynomial $f\in K[x]$, and an element $\alpha\in K$ such that the arboreal Galois representation $\rho_{f,\alpha}:\text{Gal}(\overline{K}/K)\to \text{Aut}(T_\infty)$ attached to the pair $(f,\alpha)$ is well defined, any element in the image of such representation that is a Frobenius for an unramified prime of $K$ is a settled element. We exhibit an explicit uncountable subset $S\subseteq \text{Aut}(T_\infty)$, consisting of pairwise non-conjugate settled elements, such that no matter how $K,f,\alpha$ are chosen, no element of $S$ can be a Frobenius for any ramified or unramified prime of $K$.
item.dc:creator: Andrea Ferraguti

item.title: On the average of class numbers of indefinite binary quadratic forms
item.description: arXiv:2610.28001v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that the sum of class numbers of primitive indefinite binary quadratic forms with integer coefficients over positive nonsquare discriminants less than $X$ is $O(X^{3/2}\sqrt{\log\log X}/(\log X)^{3/2})$. This improves the longstanding classical upper bound $O(X^{3/2}/\log X)$ and implies the same upper bound for the corresponding sum over real quadratic fields. Our main input is a uniform upper bound for the number of small fundamental solutions to Pell's equation. In particular, we prove that, for almost all nonsquare positive integers $D$, the fundamental solution $\varepsilon_D$ of $t^2-Du^2=1$ is larger than any fixed power of $D$.
item.dc:creator: Yijie Diao

item.title: Irrationality exponents of logarithmic numbers: Values, quotients, and graded approximation
item.description: arXiv:2610.28079v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We establish degree-dependent irrationality-exponent bounds for logarithms at algebraic arguments and sharper bounds when conjugate logarithms match. A two-torus construction gives an upper bound of three for ratios of logarithms of multiplicatively independent positive rational numbers. We also treat normalized quadratic logarithms and circular logarithms. The rational-logarithm and rational-power exponent-two cases were treated earlier by Liu, Jiang and Zhang; we retain them within the broader framework and its Lean verification. Starting from the interpolation and determinant method in OpenAI's September 24, 2026 preprint on the irrationality exponent of $\pi$, we track the arithmetic cost of algebraic embeddings and the effects of matching conjugate logarithms. A second, graded Pade construction gives near-optimal measures for powers and bounded-degree polynomial values at sufficiently small logarithmic arguments, with estimates uniform in both coefficient height and rational denominator. We state the branch, independence, parameter-order, and approximation-field hypotheses explicitly. The Lean supplement has reviewed endpoint correspondences for all 62 numbered results: 53 direct checked endpoints or compositions, and nine applications with named classical theorem inputs. Native proofs of those inputs and separate formalizations of every unnumbered assertion are not supplied. Appendix A gives the exact declarations, hypotheses, and verification evidence.
item.dc:creator: Gregory V. Chudnovsky

item.title: Simultaneous visibility in cut-and-project sets
item.description: arXiv:2610.28119v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Visibility from the origin in integer lattices is a well-studied problem. More recently, the corresponding question for cut-and-project sets has attracted attention. We consider simultaneous visibility, which asks what points in a set are visible from every point of another set. This question was studied for the integer lattice by Rearick and Rumsey, among others. In this work, we investigate simultaneous visibility in cut-and-project sets associated with real quadratic fields satisfying the Hammarhjelm condition. Under suitable geometric conditions on the finite set, we prove that the density of the simultaneously visible points exists and derive an explicit formula for it. We also examine simultaneous visibility in more general cut-and-project sets under a condition on the associated lattice.
item.dc:creator: Rishi Kumar, Carlos Ospina

item.title: Euler systems for self-dual Hecke characters over biquadratic fields with applications
item.description: arXiv:2610.28196v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We construct a new Euler system attached to a self-dual Hecke character $\chi$ over an imaginary biquadratic field $K_0$. The Euler system is anticyclotomic in the sense of Jetchev--Nekov\'a{\v r}--Skinner. As arithmetic applications, we deduce instances of the Bloch--Kato conjecture in analytic ranks $0$, $1$, and $2$ (the last one for certain CM abelian surfaces). In addition, we establish the full Iwasawa--Greenberg main conjecture for $\chi$ over $K_0$. In this biquadratic setting, our work generalizes Rubin's work on the Iwasawa main conjectures for imaginary quadratic fields using Euler systems of elliptic units, while complementing known results of Hida and Hsieh for general CM fields.
item.dc:creator: Kim Tuan Do

item.title: Simultaneous popular differences for polynomial and linear progressions in finite fields
item.description: arXiv:2610.28226v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study simultaneous popular differences for polynomial progressions and linear progressions over finite fields $\mathbb F_p$. For certain families of polynomial progressions of algebraic complexity $1$, such as $(x, x+y, x+2y)$ and $(x, x+y^3, x+2y^3)$, we prove the existence of $y \neq 0$ which is popular simultaneously for both progressions. This extends previous results by Conlon, Dong and Hong who considered complexity $0$ progressions. On the other hand, we construct counterexamples showing that simultaneous popular differences are not guaranteed to exist for $(x, x+y, x+2y)$ and $(x, x+y^2, x+2y^2)$, or for $(x, x+y, x+2y)$ and $(x, x+y, x+3y)$, or for $(x, x+y, x+2y)$ and $(x,x+y,x+2y,x+3y)$, answering questions posed by Conlon, Dong and Hong.
item.dc:creator: Xuancheng Shao, Weiwen Zhang

item.title: A necessary condition for a Romanoff type theorem
item.description: arXiv:2610.28237v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $\{a_k\}_{k\ge1}$ be an infinite strictly increasing sequence of positive integers with $a_k\mid a_{k+1}$ for every integer $k\ge1$. Dai and Pan proved that the set of integers of the form $p^2+q^2+a_k+a_l$, where $p,q$ are primes and $k,l\ge1$, has positive lower asymptotic density if $\limsup_{k\to\infty}\frac{\log a_k}{k}<\infty$ and $\sup_{k\ge1}\sum_{d\mid a_k}\frac1d<\infty$. They also asked whether the latter condition is necessary. In this paper, we show that this condition is necessary by proving that if $\sup_{k\ge1}\sum_{d\mid a_k}\frac1d=\infty$, then this set has asymptotic density zero.
item.dc:creator: Xiao-Hui Yan, Ya-Ting Xu

item.title: A Joint Local Limit Theorem for Prime Divisor Counting Functions
item.description: arXiv:2610.28328v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We establish a uniform two-dimensional local limit theorem for the joint distribution of $\Omega(n)$ and $\Omega(n+1)$. More precisely, along a set of scales of logarithmic density one, the normalized joint counts are uniformly approximated by the density of two independent Gaussian random variables, each with mean and variance $\log\log x$, up to a power-saving error. The proof builds upon a recent circle-method framework of Tao and Ter\"av\"ainen. Our results equally hold for the additive function $\omega$. Additionally, we explore applications of our local limit theorem in the setting of uniquely ergodic systems.
item.dc:creator: Jovan Andreevski

item.title: Unconditional Subexponential Arithmetic Circuits\ for Positive Factorial Multiples
item.description: arXiv:2610.28338v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $\tau(n)$ be the least number of binary additions, subtractions and multiplications required to construct $n$ from $1$ and $2$, with reuse of intermediate values. We show that, for every sufficiently large integer $k$, some positive integer $m$ satisfies \[ \tau(mk!)\leq \exp\!\left(O\!\left((\log k)^{2/3}(\log\log k)^{1/3}\right)\right). \] The proof combines unconditional results of Lenstra, Pila and Pomerance on smooth numbers in short intervals and on orders of genus-two Jacobians with a five-parameter family carrying a rational divisor class of infinite order. We encode rational divisor arithmetic, including the tests determining its branches, by a nonzero division-free integer circuit. A common finite sampling space yields circuits whose outputs collectively contain every prime at most $k$, and repeated squaring supplies the required factorial valuations. The circuit bound includes the cost of constructing all integer parameters. This work was carried out with assistance from the UniMath model, developed by UniDT (Shanghai) Co., Ltd., and GPT-6.1 Sol.
item.dc:creator: Liang Zhang (Michael), Xiaohua (Michael), Xuan

item.title: Small and large gaps between zeros of Dirichlet $L$-functions
item.description: arXiv:2610.28527v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For every fixed primitive Dirichlet $L$-function and every $\varepsilon>0$, we prove unconditionally that infinitely many consecutive zeros have spacing less than $1/2+\varepsilon$ times the mean. Assuming the Riemann Hypothesis, we also prove a positive proportion of such spacings for the Riemann zeta-function, and infinitely many spacings greater than $3.63$ times the mean for every fixed primitive Dirichlet $L$-function.
item.dc:creator: Benjamin Durkan, Andrew Pearce-Crump

item.title: Borel's computation of the ranks of $K$-theory revisited
item.description: arXiv:2610.26885v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We reprove Borel's computation of the rank of the $K$-groups of rings of algebraic integers $\mathcal{O}_F$ for certain number fields, e.g., $F = \mathbb{Q}(\mu_{l^k})$ for $l$ an odd regular prime number. The idea is to recover a simple formula for $l$-adic {\'e}tale cohomology groups of $\mathcal{O}_F$ in terms of Iwasawa theoretic objects without using Borel's result as an input.
item.dc:creator: Jan Ole Hesse

item.title: Generic distinction of induced representations: the case of symmetric spaces
item.description: arXiv:2610.27458v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let H be the fixed-point subgroup of an involution of a reductive group G over a local field F of characteristic zero. We give a necessary condition for a parabolically induced representation of G(F) to admit a non-zero family of H(F)-equivariant linear forms depending holomorphically on the induction parameter. By works of Blanc-Delorme and Brylinski-Delorme, this condition is essentially sufficient. As a global consequence, we obtain vanishing results for regularized periods of Eisenstein series. We illustrate this on symplectic periods, where we extend Offen's computation of truncated periods of certain cuspidal Eisenstein series to inner forms of GL(2n).
item.dc:creator: Pierre-Henri Chaudouard, Cheng Chen

item.title: A cut-and-project set which is not bi-Lipschitz equivalent to a lattice
item.description: arXiv:2610.27640v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We construct a cut-and-project set in a totally irrational plane in $\mathbb{R}^3$, with a compact window which is the closure of its interior and has countable boundary, which is not bi-Lipschitz equivalent to a lattice. This answers a question of Burago and Kleiner about cut-and-project sets, and shows in particular that the hypothesis of boundary measure zero is not enough to guarantee bi-Lipschitz equivalence to a lattice. Since our set has uniform density, it also shows that a non-rectifiable Delone set need not encode a non-realisable density, answering a question of Bhat and Dymond.
item.dc:creator: Alan Haynes

item.title: Rational analytic prismatization
item.description: arXiv:2610.27918v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We develop a general theory of analytic prismatization with $\mathbb{Q}_p$-coefficients in rigid analytic geometry over $\mathbb{Q}_p$. We prove an equivalence of perfect complexes on the perfect analytic prismatization modulo Frobenius with perfect complexes on the relative Fargues--Fontaine curve for any smooth partially proper rigid analytic variety. In particular, we explain how this equivalence conceptualizes the decompletion techniques by passing to locally analytic vectors which appear in (geometric) Sen theory
item.dc:creator: Johannes Ansch\"utz, Arthur-C\'esar Le Bras, Juan Esteban Rodr\'iguez Camargo, Peter Scholze

item.title: Supercuspidal blocks and the local Langlands correspondence
item.description: arXiv:2610.27924v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $G$ be a connected reductive group defined over a non-archimedean local field $F$, and let $\mathrm{Rep}^{\mathfrak{s}}(G(F))$ be a supercuspidal Bernstein block. In this paper, we define a cohomology class $[\mu_{\mathfrak{s}}]$ represented by a 2-cocycle that encodes the equivalence class of $\mathrm{Rep}^{\mathfrak{s}}(G(F))$. We then formulate a conjecture describing $[\mu_{\mathfrak{s}}]$ in terms of the enhanced $L$-parameter $(\varphi, \rho)$ attached to an irreducible representation in $\mathrm{Rep}^{\mathfrak{s}}(G(F))$ via the conjectural local Langlands correspondence. Finally, we verify this conjecture for the local Langlands correspondence for non-singular supercuspidal representations constructed by Kaletha.
item.dc:creator: Noriyuki Abe, Kazuma Ohara

item.title: The stacky approach to de Rham-Witt cohomology
item.description: arXiv:2610.28149v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $k$ be a perfect field of characteristic $p>0$. Ekedahl proved an equivalence of triangulated categories between bounded coherent complexes over the Raynaud ring and complexes of $F$-gauges. We give a geometric proof, independent of his proof, that the de Rham-Witt realization is a symmetric monoidal equivalence of stable $\infty$-categories between perfect $F$-gauges and bounded coherent complexes over the Raynaud ring with Ekedahl's completed star product, as expected by Illusie. The geometry comes from topological restriction homology: $\mathrm{TR}^r(k;\mathbf Z_p)^{hS^1}$ is an iterated fibre product of copies of $\mathrm{TC}^-(k;\mathbf Z_p)$, and taking even stacks before and after the fibre product gives the genuine and the naive $r$-Nygaard stacks. Pushforward from the genuine to the naive $r$-Nygaard stack realizes Andriopoulos' $r$-Nygaard filtrations, which interpolate between the Nygaard filtration at $r=1$ and the Hodge-Witt filtration at $r=\infty$. On the genuine $r$-Nygaard stack, which is a chain of Nygaard charts, restriction and Frobenius come from the inclusions of sub-chains, Verschiebung from duality, and the differential as a Bockstein operator, and the relations of the star product become projection formulas. As applications, we deduce Ekedahl's K\"unneth formula and Poincar\'e duality for de Rham-Witt cohomology from their counterparts for $F$-gauge cohomology, and show that the special-value formulas of Illusie and of Mondal over finite fields are equivalent.
item.dc:creator: Yuanning Zhang

item.title: Effective existence of primitive k-normal elements via affine spaces
item.description: arXiv:2510.26972v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $\mathbb{F}_{q^n}$ be the finite field with $q^n$ elements. An element $\alpha \in \mathbb{F}_{q^n}$ is $k$-normal over $\mathbb{F}_q$ if $\alpha$ and its conjugates span an $\mathbb{F}_q$-subspace of dimension $n-k$. It is known that, for $q$ sufficiently large, a primitive $k$-normal element exists if and only if there exists a $k$-normal element free of binomials, but the lower bound on $q$ is not explicit. We count the $k$-normal elements in specific affine subspaces of $\mathbb{F}_{q^n}$ and show that, in some of them, all but at most one element is $k$-normal. Combining this with character sum estimates over affine spaces and a sieve, we obtain an explicit lower bound on $q$ above which a primitive $k$-normal element exists, provided there is a $k$-normal element free of binomials whose $\mathbb{F}_q$-order has a linear factor or is irreducible. As an application, we compute these bounds for $5 \le n \le 8$ and give a complete characterization of the existence of primitive $k$-normal elements in $\mathbb{F}_{q^6}$ over $\mathbb{F}_q$.
item.dc:creator: Josimar J. R. Aguirre, Sarah F. M. Mazzini, Victor G. L. Neumann

item.title: Notes on the multiplier systems of $\eta(\tau)$ and $\theta(\tau)$
item.description: arXiv:2512.08187v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The multiplier systems of $\eta^{2k}(\tau)$ and $\theta^{2k}(\tau)$ $(k\in\mathbb{Z})$ are characters. In this paper, we determine their kernels, Ker$\,\nu_{\eta^{2k}}$ and Ker$\,\nu_{ \theta^{2k} } $.
item.dc:creator: Kazuhide Matsuda

item.title: On the distribution of shapes of octic Kummer extensions
item.description: arXiv:2602.12621v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The shape of a number field $K$ of degree $n$ is defined as the equivalence class of the lattice of integers under linear operations generated by rotations, reflections, and positive scalar dilations. It may be viewed as a point in the space of shapes $\mathscr{S}_{n-1} = \mathrm{GL}_{n-1}(\mathbb{Z})\backslash \mathrm{GL}_{n-1}(\mathbb{R})/\mathrm{GO}_{n-1}(\mathbb{R})$. In this paper, we study the distribution of shapes of octic Kummer extensions $L=\mathbb{Q}(i,\sqrt[4]{m})$, where $m\in\mathbb{Z}[i]$ is fourth-power-free. We parametrize these shapes by explicit invariants known as shape parameters and establish an asymptotic formula for their joint distribution ordered by absolute discriminant. The limiting distribution is given by an explicit measure that factors as the product of a continuous measure and a discrete measure arising from local arithmetic conditions.
item.dc:creator: Anuj Jakhar, Anwesh Ray

item.title: Analogue of the theta group $\Gamma_{\theta}$
item.description: arXiv:2602.22471v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we introduce higher level versions of the theta group $\Gamma_{\theta}.$ In particular, we treat level 3 and 4 versions of the theta group, $\Gamma_{\theta,3}$ and $\Gamma_{\theta,4}$ and prove that $\displaystyle F(\tau)=\eta \left(\frac{\tau-1}{3} \right) \eta\left(\frac{\tau+1}{3} \right)$ and $\displaystyle G(\tau)=\eta \left(\frac{\tau-1}{4} \right) \eta\left(\frac{\tau+1}{4} \right)$ are modular forms on $\Gamma_{\theta,3}$ and $\Gamma_{\theta,4}$ respectively. Moreover we compute their multiplier systems, $\nu_{F}$ and $\nu_{G}$.
item.dc:creator: Kazuhide Matsuda

item.title: Analogue of the theta group $\Gamma_{\theta},$ II
item.description: arXiv:2603.16109v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this series of papers, we introduce higher level versions of the theta group $\Gamma_{\theta}.$ In this paper, we treat the theta group of level $5$, $\Gamma_{\theta,5},$ and construct modular forms on $\Gamma_{\theta,5}$. Moreover we compute their multiplier systems. For this purpose, we derive transformation formula of theta function with characteristics.
item.dc:creator: Kazuhide Matsuda

item.title: The distribution of $k$-free ideals in ray class groups
item.description: arXiv:2608.13509v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we extend the classical problem of studying the distribution of $k$-free integers in arithmetic progressions to the setting of arbitrary number fields. Using the language of ray class groups, we establish asymptotic formulas, together with error terms, for the number of $k$-free ideals of bounded norm lying in a given ray class. In particular, our results show that $k$-free ideals are equidistributed among ray classes. We also obtain improved error estimates in the cases of ideal class groups and narrow class groups by using sharper ideal counting asymptotics due to Landau. Our results recover the classical formulas of Gegenbauer and Cohen--Robinson over $\mathbb{Q}$ and extend previous work of Benkowski, Nymann, and Sittinger to the setting of ray class groups. We also present explicit computational examples that illustrate the asymptotic formulas and the equidistribution of $k$-free ideals among ray classes.
item.dc:creator: Adrian Barquero-Sanchez, Jack Heimrath, Bernd Sing, Nicol\'as Sirolli, Caylee Spivey, Michael Wijaya

item.title: Shimura curves of discriminant 14 and 15 and associated Heun Functions
item.description: arXiv:2608.14495v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the Shimura curves $X_D^*(1)$ of discriminant $D$ for $D=14, 15$ relating specific weight $4$ modular forms on these Shimura curves to the associated Heun functions for the quadrilateral group. We also discuss how the Picard-Fuchs equation of the associated family of abelian surfaces has solutions coming from modular forms on $X^*_{D}(1)$. We determine the rational exceptional sets of the associated Heun functions, and the algebraic values attained by the Heun function at these points. For example, $${\rm He}\left( 81, \frac{1}{2}; \frac{1}{3}, \frac{1}{6}, \frac{1}{2}, \frac{1}{2};-\frac{729}{112}\right)= \left( \frac{2^2 \cdot 3^3 \cdot 5^3}{7^5} \right)^{\frac{1}{6}} $$.
item.dc:creator: Harshavardhan Reddy, Devendra Tiwari

item.title: An alternating Mizuno formula, modified gamma functions, and double sine special values
item.description: arXiv:2608.17545v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: For $n\ge1$ and $\operatorname{Re}(x_j)>0$, we prove an alternating analogue of Mizuno's product formula: \begin{equation*} \prod\nolimits_{m=0}^{\infty} \left(\prod_{j=1}^{n}(m+x_j)\right)^{(-1)^m} = \frac{(\sqrt{\pi/2})^n} {\prod_{j=1}^{n}\widetilde{\Gamma}(x_j)}, \end{equation*} where $\widetilde{\Gamma}$ is the modified gamma function associated with the alternating Hurwitz zeta function. The polynomial factors are regularized using factorwise logarithms, and the formula establishes compatibility between this regularization and polynomial factorization. Applications include Gaussian and cyclotomic (Kurokawa--Wakayama type) evaluations; the single-factor case recovers the alternating Lerch formula, and a normalized ratio yields Wallis' product. A second group of results concerns an alternating double sine-type function. At nonexceptional positive periods, its positive-integer special values admit finite tangent-product representations. These products define locally meromorphic continuations $F_m$ in the period parameter. For $m\ge2$ and nonzero algebraic parameters, the continued values belong to $\mathbb P^1(\overline{\mathbb Q})$ at rational parameters and are finite, nonzero, and transcendental at nonrational parameters. We determine their orders at rational parameters and distinguish parameter continuation from fixed-period specialization at exceptional parameters. Additional results include Barnes factorizations of multiple alternating gamma functions, a Glaisher--Kinkelin special value, finite-product Stirling-type asymptotics, a symmetric two-parameter form of the known odd-integer multiplication formula, and an odd-scaling distribution relation for the alternating double sine-type function.
item.dc:creator: Su Hu, Min-Soo Kim

item.title: On lifting representations and actions on curves of the metacyclic groups $C_{p^s}\rtimes C_m$
item.description: arXiv:2609.03191v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: For a prime $p$, a pair $(s,m)\in\mathbb{N}^2$ with $m$ relatively prime to $p$, a homomorphism $\chi:C_m\rightarrow\operatorname{Aut}(C_{p^s})$, and an algebraically closed field $k$ of characteristic $p$, we consider the semidirect product $G=C_{p^s}\rtimes_{\chi} C_m$, the $p$-Sylow subgroup $H\cong C_{p^s}$ of $G$, and a $k[G]$-module $V$. Let $R$ be a complete discrete valuation ring of residue field $k$ and mixed characteristic $(0,p)$ that contains a primitive $p^s$-th root of unity. If $\chi$ is injective, we present two necessary and sufficient criteria for lifting $V$ to an $R[G]$-module $\widetilde{V}$ which is a free $R$-module: (i) when no extra requirement is made on $\widetilde{V}$ and (ii) when we require $\widetilde{V}^H=\{0\}$. The criteria correct several results in the literature and we use them to prove that, if $\chi$ is injective and $G$ acts faithfully on a connected smooth projective curve $X$ over $k$, then, under mild hypotheses satisfied if $X\rightarrow X/G$ is a Harbater--Katz--Gabber cover, the $k[G]$-module $H^0(X,\Omega_X)$ has a lift $\widetilde{V}$ to $R$ with $\widetilde{V}^H=\{0\}$. Also, with $B:=R[\frac{1}{p}]$, we prove the following obstruction when $p$ is odd, $m$ is even, $\chi$ is injective, and $X/C_{p^s}\cong\mathbb{P}^1_k$: if no such lift $\widetilde{V}$ exists with the $B[H]$-module $\widetilde{V}\otimes_R B$ defined over $\mathbb{Q}$, then the action of $G$ on $X$ does not lift to $R$.
item.dc:creator: Huy Dang, Adrian Vasiu

item.title: Eigenvectors of $p$-Curvature for Geometric Difference Equations
item.description: arXiv:2609.21090v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: A qKZ-type additive discrete flat connection in characteristic $p$ has $p$-curvature operators. They are commuting automorphisms of the connection. We present a Bethe-ansatz-type construction of eigensections and eigenvalues of the $p$-curvature operators. An eigensection of $p$-curvature operators is a discrete hypergeometric sum over the finite lattice $\mathbb{Z}^r/p\mathbb{Z}^r$. Thus, the $p$-curvature eigensections are constructed by a finite, discrete analogue of a hypergeometric integral.
item.dc:creator: Vitaly Tarasov, Alexander Varchenko

item.title: Transcendence of dendric beta-expansions with pure discrete spectrum
item.description: arXiv:2610.00856v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove the transcendence of numbers that have $\beta$-expansions (in algebraic bases $\beta$) belonging to dendric shifts with pure discrete spectrum, under combinatorial conditions on their directive sequences of substitutions. This includes Arnoux-Rauzy sequences on arbitrary alphabets and Cassaigne-Selmer sequences. The proof uses Rauzy fractals and the subspace theorem.
item.dc:creator: Jihyuk Seo, Wolfgang Steiner

item.title: Idempotence in Carmichael and Giuga numbers and its application to the Agoh-Giuga conjecture
item.description: arXiv:2610.09129v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This article analyzes the idempotence of Giuga numbers and Carmichael numbers. The first sections will lead us to define an arithmetic function through which we will find a new characterization of Giuga numbers. The following sections will lead us to generalize Carmichael numbers, finding numbers that are Fermat pseudoprimes in certain specific cases, and to formulate various statements and open questions regarding their properties. Finally, we will find a new alternative condition, based on idempotence, that a number must satisfy to be a counterexample to the Agoh-Giuga conjecture and which, therefore, presumably, no number will ever satisfy. We will almost always work under the premise that n is square-free, since both numbers always have that property, but in certain situations we will extend some of the results to the general case.
item.dc:creator: Miguel \'Angel L\'opez

item.title: On a Digital Signature Based on Matrix Decomposition and the MinRank Problem
item.description: arXiv:2610.09140v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The following article attempts to define a new digital signature scheme based on a variant of the MinRank problem under appropriate parameters. First, the key generation process will be defined, followed by the message signing and verification processes. The speed of signing and verification will be analyzed, and finally, the signature will be evaluated in terms of security and robustness against known attacks, which will lead to a set of requirements that we will consider when selecting certain parameters related to the size and number of variables. It should be noted that this signature, although simple in design, can serve as the foundation for an entire family of digital signatures based on the central idea that inspired its creation.
item.dc:creator: Miguel \'Angel L\'opez

item.title: The Density and Quantitative Upper Bound of Integers Not Expressible as the Sum of a Prime and a Zumkeller Number
item.description: arXiv:2610.19574v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: A Zumkeller number is a positive integer whose set of positive divisors can be partitioned into two disjoint subsets of equal sums. In this paper, we investigate the additive properties of these numbers in conjunction with prime numbers. Specifically, we study the natural density of the exceptional set \(\mathcal{E}\) consisting of all positive integers not expressible as the sum of a prime and a Zumkeller number. Let $\alpha(x) = \#\{n \le x : n \in \mathcal{E}\}$ denote its counting function. We establish a quantitative upper bound for $\alpha(x)$, demonstrating that $\alpha(x) \ll x(\log \log x)^{-A}$, where $A = \log_2\left(\frac{2\pi^2}{2\pi^2-3}\right) \approx 0.2378$, thereby proving that the natural density of this exceptional set is $0$.
item.dc:creator: Ting Hon Stanford Li

item.title: Sign bias in hyperbolic double cosets
item.description: arXiv:2610.26462v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study sign bias between hyperbolic double cosets with $ad>0$ and $ad<0$ in appropriate cocompact Fuchsian groups. We prove that an eventual bias can only favour $ad<0$, and show that such a bias occurs within every cocompact Fuchsian commensurability class. When the normal-derivative periods of all nonconstant eigenfunctions with eigenvalue at most $1/4$ vanish, we prove an $\Omega_\pm(X^{1/2})$ result and show that the counting difference takes both signs in every sufficiently large interval $[X,CX]$, for some fixed $C>1$.
item.dc:creator: Marios Voskou

item.title: On multilinear forms for mod $p$ representations of $\operatorname{GL}_2$ over a $p$-adic field
item.description: arXiv:2610.26541v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $F$ be a finite extension of $\mathbb Q_p$, for any prime $p$, and let $L/F$ be a ramified quadratic extension. We compute the spaces of $\mathcal O_L^\times$-equivariant linear forms on the representation $\operatorname{ind}^G_{KZ}\sigma/(\Phi-\lambda)$. The only nonzero cases arise from one-dimensional quotients. Consequently, the restriction of an infinite-dimensional irreducible smooth mod $p$ representation of $\operatorname{GL}_2(F)$ with a central character to $\mathcal O_L^\times$ has no character quotient. We apply this vanishing result to show that a finite tensor product of smooth mod $p$ representations of $\operatorname{GL}_2(F)$ admits no nonzero invariant linear form whenever at least one factor is infinite-dimensional and irreducible with a central character.
item.dc:creator: Hao Liu, Haoran Wang, Yuting Yang

item.title: A cluster criterion for potential degeneracy of superelliptic curves
item.description: arXiv:2508.15974v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Let $K$ be a field with a discrete valuation; let $p$ be a prime; and let $C$ be the curve defined by an equation of the form $y^p = f(x)$. We show that the curve $C$ has a model over an algebraic extension of $K$ whose special fiber consists of genus-$0$ components and has at worst nodal singularities if and only if the cluster data of the roots of $f$ satisfies a certain criterion, and when these hold, we show explicitly how to build the minimal regular model of $C$. We develop an interpretation of cluster data in terms of a convex hull in the Berkovich projective line and express the above results directly in terms of this convex hull.
item.dc:creator: Jeffrey Yelton

item.title: A note on complex Lie Algebras isomorphic to their conjugate
item.description: arXiv:2604.06979v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: A real Lie algebra defines by extension of scalars a complex Lie algebra that is isomorphic to its Galois conjugate. In this paper, we are interested in the converse property: given a complex Lie algebra that is isomorphic to its conjugate, is it defined over the real numbers? We prove the existence of a $10$-dimensional nilpotent complex Lie algebra for which the answer is negative, disproving a recent conjecture by Der\'e. In addition, we compute the generic obstruction to this descent problem in terms of Brauer groups.
item.dc:creator: Cyril Demarche

item.title: Sharp Threshold for Universality of Rational Canonical Forms over a Finite Field
item.description: arXiv:2609.01413v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study the rational canonical form of sparse random matrices over a finite field. Suppose $A_n\in\mathrm{Mat}_n(\mathbb{F}_p)$ has independent and $\alpha_n$-balanced entries. We prove that if $n\alpha_n-\log n\to+\infty$, then, for every fixed collection of distinct monic irreducible polynomials over $\mathbb{F}_p$, the corresponding primary partitions of $A_n$ converge jointly to the same asymptotically independent Cohen-Lenstra distributions as in the uniform random matrix model. This strengthens the finite-field cokernel universality theorem of Lee (arXiv:2511.13070), which assumes $\alpha_n=c\log n/n$ for a fixed $c>1$, by resolving the additive endpoint case explicitly left open in his work. Moreover, our result extends universality from ordinary cokernels to the full rational canonical form. The condition is optimal for universality uniformly over fixed irreducible polynomials. Our proof uses the surjection moment method developed by Sawin and Wood (arXiv:2210.06279) over $\mathbb{F}_p[t]$, together with a refinement of Lee's Fourier estimates that retains the full leading-order decay. We also construct degree-$d$ critical sparse obstructions, suggesting a polynomial-dependent threshold of $1/d$ for irreducible polynomials of minimal degree $d$.
item.dc:creator: Jiahe Shen

item.title: Integral trace duality and the Witt filtration on Lubin--Tate space
item.description: arXiv:2610.18246v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Let $\mathcal O$ be the Lubin--Tate deformation ring of a one-dimensional commutative formal group of finite height $n\geq1$ over a perfect field $k$ of characteristic $p$. We identify Rezk's Witt filtration $\{I_d\}$ with the divisibility filtration of integral trace pairings on subgroup algebras of fixed source lifts. This gives the geometric recursion \[ I_{d+1}=pI_d+J_{d,z}\qquad(d\geq0), \] where $J_{d,z}$ defines the targets of order-$p^d$ quotient isogenies from a $W(k)$-valued lift $z$ of the closed point. The corrected ideal is independent of $z$. We also compute the cokernel of the universal source trace pairing over $\mathcal O$: it is $\bigoplus_{j=1}^d(\mathcal O/p^j)^{r_j-r_{j-1}}$, where $r_j$ counts order-$p^j$ subgroups of $(\mathbf Q_p/\mathbf Z_p)^n$. The same duality extends the generic trace along two-step isogeny flags to an integral surjection, even when the flag-forgetting map is not flat. This computes composition in the subring of weighted trace operations. Applications include sharp projector denominators and congruence fibre products for full-torsion loci.
item.dc:creator: Andrea Taccani

item.title: Reciprocal Dynamics in Polynomial Congruence Jumping: Integral Orbits and Valuation Cones
item.description: arXiv:2610.20176v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Alternating reciprocal transformations of polynomial divisibility systems couple an orbit of integer points to a rational dynamical system on polynomial coefficients. For fixed positive degrees $n,m$, we prove universal four-step return to rational gauge classes. Weighted primitive representatives preserve integral continuation through nondegenerate jumps using only exact division and coefficient gcds; the stronger requirement of monic integral representatives is governed by endpoint $p$-adic valuation defects. After one integral block, constant-term valuations evolve by an explicit unimodular matrix whose trace depends only on $nm$. This gives finite-order behavior for $nm<4$, parabolic dilations for $nm=4$, and hyperbolic dynamics for $nm>4$. In the hyperbolic case, invariant thresholds, irrational eigencones, and discrete valley formulas give finite criteria for forward and bi-infinite integral coefficient orbits, although failure can be delayed arbitrarily long. Every positive-constant canonical monic coefficient chain admits an explicit positive rational four-phase gauge. At $nm=4$, geometric gauges reduce nondegenerate compatible rational point orbits to two-periodic affine recurrences, hence to sequences satisfying linear recurrences with constant coefficients. Polynomial identities of degree at most $h$ on each invariant conic admit certificates from $2h+1$ initial phase states, while integral unimodular recurrence models yield periodic modular obstructions. For $nm>4$, eventually positive normalized point orbits tending to infinity have hyperbolic logarithmic growth and cannot satisfy such linear recurrences. Finally, separated auxiliary-relation transport reduces rational rank to at most one after two alternating jumps; quadratic specialization gives exact local saturation criteria and persistence results across periodic, parabolic, and hyperbolic orbits.
item.dc:creator: Max A. Alekseyev, Dmitry I. Khomovsky

item.title: A Simple Proof of I. Chowla's Theorem on Addition of Residue Classes
item.description: arXiv:2610.22427v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We present a brief, elementary proof of a striking theorem by I. Chowla on the addition of residue classes (1937) which generalizes the famous result of Cauchy and Davenport to residue classes modulo a composite.
item.dc:creator: Drew Duncan
